# A Data-worker pipeline loads an app's own stage classes by modulePath

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs. Curated because the change is bounded, has a merged precedent in the same file (the interceptor descriptors of #9553) and needs no private context.

## Context

Found while building the data pipeline example (#21880, PR #21950). The example's own shaping, a report over a million orders, had to live in a `postParse` interceptor: an interceptor is the only app class a pipeline can run in the Data worker. It is finding 4 of that ticket's intake comment and was promised as its own ticket in the PR body.

Read from source at `dev` `5f3efca9da` and from the guide; not run. AC-1's first spec is the run.

Live latest-open + closed sweep: checked the latest 20 open plus open and closed searches (`loadDataModule`, `pipeline modulePath`, `custom parser data worker`, `normalizer workerExecution`; ledgers of #9553, #9551 and #9453 read) at 2026-11-22T14:46Z; no equivalent and no prior exclusion found. Backlog band: 87 open, red; no open ticket or epic owns the pipeline's remote setup, so this is filed. A2A claims since 02:00Z: none on this scope. Memory Core: one query on the symptom, no prior decision. Own open tickets: #21880 is the only one on this surface.

## The Problem

`workerExecution: 'data'` moves a pipeline's connection, parser and normalizer into the Data worker, so that heavy shaping costs the app nothing. That holds only for the engine's own classes:

- `Pipeline#createRemoteExecution` preloads the three stages with `Neo.worker.Data.loadDataModule({className})` (`src/data/Pipeline.mjs` L520-L528).
- `loadDataModule` answers `{success: false, error: 'Not a Neo.data class'}` for any other namespace and imports only from `src/data/connection`, `parser` and `normalizer` (`src/worker/Data.mjs` from L180).
- The three results are awaited and never read (`Pipeline.mjs` L533-L535), so a refused class surfaces later and elsewhere, if at all.

An app with its own format, record shape or transport therefore keeps that work on the App worker, or bends it into an interceptor hook. The guide promises more: "to unlock advanced features like Data Worker offloading (`workerExecution: 'data'`) or custom Parsers" (`learn/guides/datahandling/DataPipelines.md` L389), and its note on Data execution asks for `className` strings without saying which classes qualify (L126).

## The Architectural Reality

- The Data worker already loads app code through a scoped loader: `importAppSpaceModule` admits `apps/`, `examples/`, `docs/app/` and `src/data/` (`src/worker/Data.mjs` L101-L136), and `loadModule({path, className})` imports through it and checks the exported class (L237-L252). `createInstance`'s JSDoc names the purpose: "avoiding the loading of heavy data-shaping logic (like Parsers/Normalizers) inside the App Worker".
- Interceptors use exactly that route: a descriptor carries `className` and `modulePath`, `InterceptorChain.validateDescriptors` refuses any path that is not a scoped, non-escaping `.mjs` path (`src/data/interceptor/Chain.mjs` L90-L95), and `Pipeline.preloadInterceptors` throws on a failed load (`Pipeline.mjs` L70-L79).
- `loadDataModule` is folder-scoped on purpose: it keeps webpack's context to three folders.

Design authority: the interceptor descriptor contract of #9553 ("serialized Data descriptors carry `className` and `modulePath`", "Check preload results and exported class identity").

## The Fix

In `src/data/Pipeline.mjs`, `createRemoteExecution` treats a stage config as it treats an interceptor descriptor:

1. A `connection`, `parser` or `normalizer` config may carry `modulePath`. It passes the same rule as an interceptor's path, as one shared function, not a copy.
2. With `modulePath`, the stage is preloaded by `Neo.worker.Data.loadModule({path, className})`; without it, a `Neo.data.*` class goes through `loadDataModule` as today.
3. Every preload result is read. A refusal fails the remote setup with an error that names the class and the loader's reason; a class outside `Neo.data` without `modulePath` fails before any worker call, naming `modulePath`.
4. `modulePath` does not reach the stage instance as a config (interceptors strip it, `Chain.mjs` L159).

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Pipeline#connection`, `#parser`, `#normalizer` with `workerExecution: 'data'` | `createRemoteExecution`; the interceptor descriptor of #9553 | a config with `className` and `modulePath` loads the app's class in the Data worker and runs it there | no `modulePath`: `Neo.data.*` as today; any other class is refused with a named error | `DataPipelines.md` §2; the three configs' JSDoc | unit spec on the remote setup; one e2e spec with a class under `examples/` |
| `modulePath` on a stage config | `InterceptorChain.validateDescriptors` | the same roots and the same refusals as an interceptor's | `TypeError` before any worker call | same | unit arms per refused form |
| a stage preload that fails | `Pipeline.preloadInterceptors` | the remote setup rejects, naming class and reason | none | JSDoc of `createRemoteExecution` | unit arm with a refusing worker stub |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with` the pipeline's interceptor contract (#9553); no ADR is touched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: With `workerExecution: 'data'`, a pipeline whose parser is `{className, modulePath}` under `examples/` loads that module in the Data worker and its output reaches the store; the same holds for a connection and a normalizer. A unit spec covers the three preload calls; one e2e spec runs a real class. The e2e spec is written first and recorded red on `dev`, with what a user sees today.
- [ ] AC-2: A stage `modulePath` outside the four roots, with a `..` segment, a query or a control character is refused before any worker call, by the function the interceptor chain uses.
- [ ] AC-3: A stage the Data worker cannot load rejects the remote setup with an error naming the class and the reason, for a non-`Neo.data` class without `modulePath` and for a loader refusal.
- [ ] AC-4: Pipelines with `Neo.data.*` stages and no `modulePath` behave as before; the existing pipeline specs stay green.
- [ ] AC-5: `DataPipelines.md` §2 shows the custom-stage form beside its `className` note, and the three configs' JSDoc names `modulePath`.

## Out of Scope

- Loading a stage by `modulePath` on the App worker: there the class is imported as today.
- The `examples/data/pipeline` example (PR #21950). Moving its report from the interceptor into a normalizer is a natural follow-up once this lands.
- Widening `loadDataModule`.

## Avoided Traps

- Letting `loadDataModule` accept any namespace: it would widen a webpack context that is scoped on purpose, and it has no path to import from.
- Sending a class, an instance or a function across the worker boundary: only data options cross it, as for interceptors.

## Related

- #21880 and PR #21950, where the gap was met.
- #9553, the interceptor system this mirrors.
